transcript.prompt: Draw 1 of 60: a red ball appears. You have 1 keep(s) left. KEEP or PASS?
transcript.reply:
I'll analyze this strategically. With only 1 keep available across 60 draws and 8 colors total, I need to decide whether to commit to red now or wait for more information about color frequencies.

Since this is the very first draw, I have no data yet on which colors are common. The expected value of keeping red depends on how many red balls remain in the bag. If red appears frequently, keeping it now guarantees I capture all of them. If red is rare, I might be better off passing and waiting to see other colors.

However, keeping immediately locks in red's entire frequency, which could be substantial. The -10 cost is a one-time penalty, so the break-even point is just 11 red balls total (10 + 1 for the kept ball itself).

Given the uncertainty and that I'll only see ~7.5 balls per color on average (60/8), I should gather more information before committing my single keep.

DECISION: PASS

transcript.reply:
I've now seen 2 different colors in 2 draws. With 8 colors total and 58 draws remaining, I still have minimal information about which colors are frequent.

Passing again allows me to see more of the distribution before committing. Since I can only keep once, I want to maximize the probability of keeping a color that appears many times. The expected frequency per color is 60/8 = 7.5 balls, so I need a color to appear significantly more than that to make keeping worthwhile given the -10 penalty.

I should wait to see a pattern emerge - if a color appears multiple times in the next several draws, that's a signal it might be common enough to keep.

DECISION: PASS

I don't yet have any signal about which colors are common. Passing allows me to continue observing the distribution - if I see a color repeat soon, that's evidence it might be frequent enough to keep. The cost of committing now to an unknown color outweighs the benefit.
